issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineJobs.swift:765-781 (followSweptHolders only checks and follows the sweep's own space-parked candidates); EngineJobs.swift:686-688 (doc: 'judges each job as the follow leaves it, at the place the pump would serve it from'); docs/adr-drafts/s3f.md:989-995 and :2123-2127 ('Not changed' / 'Not verified here', recorded with a rationale); the proposed §7.10 text at s3f.md:1677-1684
issues.problem:
The pre-phase follows only space-parked candidates that hold a moved id. If the holder of a moved id is downloading or queued, its follow visit is still owed when the sweep judges. The parked job of that id's new content is then judged at its pre-follow prefetch place, which is the same defect as cycle-7 PROMOTE.

Probe PROBE-C8R-INFLIGHT-PROMOTE (/Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-orchestrator/s3f-probes-c8/reqs/VerifyC8ReqsProbes.swift) uses the committed PROMOTE setup with two changes:
- C (5 MB) is downloading, held by the source. A is its user waiter and B its prefetch waiter (same content), so the follow keeps C running.
- 7 MB of room is left, so R (3.5 MB, earlier ticket) and P (3 MB) wait awaitingSpace behind C's in-flight bytes.
v3 moves A onto P while the bounded follow owes C's visit. The reclaim then leaves 6 MB beside C.

At HEAD 40ecd95, 3 of 3 runs (debug, scratch copy):
- sweepFollowsFirst: R is judged first and served; P is parked. A's user waiter gets `failure(insufficientSpace(required: 3000000, available: 2500000))` (VerifyC8ReqsProbes.swift:114:9: 'Expectation failed: (try? aResult.get())?.byteSize == Int64(pBytes.count)'), the same figures as cycle-7 PROMOTE. P's prefetch waiter gets the same failure.
- followVisitedFirst: P ranks 0. A and P are served (3 MB); R gets insufficientSpace(required: 3500000, available: 3000000).
- invariantViolations() is empty in both visits.

At s3-base the follow moved every interest in the apply's turn, so this window did not exist.

The draft's rationale is that the moved interest arrives later 'as a request made at that moment would be'. By then the sweep has already handed the room to prefetch work ahead of the user work the owed follow was about to create. The outcome depends on the visit order, the criterion that made cycles 2-7 blocking. The doc comment and the §7.10 proposal claim more than the code does.
issues.fix:
Failing test first: commit PROBE-C8R-INFLIGHT-PROMOTE as an R-SYN-11 test in EngineSweepOrderTests.swift with LaneDropVisit.allCases, plus a variant where the holder is queued behind the follow rather than downloading. Assert A's user waiter is answered from P's 3 MB in both visits and R gets insufficientSpace with available < required.

Then extend the pre-phase:
- While a follow is owed, before collecting and ordering, bring forward the follow's visit (followBeforeActing) for every job, in any state, that holds a moved id whose transfer in the copy is a space-parked candidate's.
- Draw these from state.unfollowed, within the same followsPerTurn bound and .bounded exit.
- A simpler alternative: a sweep judges nothing while such a holder is unvisited and leaves it to its follow-up sweep.

Afterwards:
- Re-measure BenchSync reclaimDuringFollowTurns at 10,000 (S3-R5).
- Correct the doc comment at EngineJobs.swift:686-702, the §7.10 proposal and 'Not verified here'.
- Re-run the cycle-7 probes and the mutants noReorder, boundedJudges and requeueNoAhead.

If the orchestrator instead accepts the recorded rationale, it should rule so explicitly, and the doc claims must be narrowed to space-parked holders.

issues.area: correctness (R-SYN-11, F-28; the pre-follow-place class of cycles 2-7). The space sweep judges a job that holds a DROPPED id at its pre-follow place and lane
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFollow.swift:115-121 (holdsMovedID: `?? false` excludes ids the copy does not list); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineJobs.swift:765-783 (followSweptHolders follows only holdsMovedID jobs), :785-833 (judgeSpaceParked judges the unfollowed job at its user rank and volume), :851-858 (requeueSwept counts it ahead and records it in spaceAdmitted although it cannot start); doc claim :697-698 ('Following first gives the outcome the sweep gives when the follow visited those jobs before it')
issues.problem:
How it fails: v3 drops A's id. A's job C is space-parked and holds no moved id, so the pre-phase does not follow it. C keeps its user lane from A. It is judged at its user place, before K, on the important volume. The pump will never start C before the follow ends (`awaitsFollow` is true), and the follow's visit will end A's interest with `.notFound` and supersede C or lower it.

Probes are in /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-orchestrator/s3f-probes-c8/correct/VerifyC8CorrectProbes.swift. Each uses the RANK-ADMIT harness with the follow's turns held, and compares visit-first with sweep-first. At HEAD 40ecd95 in debug, the sweep-first cases fail 3 of 3 runs for DROPPED and DROPPED-KEEP and 2 of 2 for DROPPED-LANE; every visit-first case passes.

(1) PROBE-C8-DROPPED:
- Setup: C is 5 MB, wanted only by A (user waiter). K is 3 MB with a user waiter. Room after the reclaim is just under 6 MB.
- Sweep-first: C is re-queued and counted ahead (cAdmitted: true, C .queued). K's user waiter gets `failure(insufficientSpace(required: 3000000, available: 999000))` (VerifyC8CorrectProbes.swift:182:9).
- Visit-first: K gets success.

(2) PROBE-C8-DROPPED-KEEP:
- Setup: as DROPPED, but B (a prefetch waiter) also wants C, and v3 keeps B's id. C's user lane comes only from the dropped id.
- Sweep-first: same false shortage for K, and B's prefetch job takes the room (B gets success).
- Visit-first: K gets success, and B gets insufficientSpace(5000000, 2999000).

(3) PROBE-C8-DROPPED-LANE:
- Setup: 26 / 34 MB capacities, so the reclaim leaves 4 MB important and 12 MB opportunistic.
- Sweep-first: C is judged on the important volume, does not fit and is parked. B's prefetch waiter gets `insufficientSpace(required: 5000000, available: 4000078)` (:178:17). A gets that shortage too instead of `.notFound` (:187:13).
- Visit-first: C is prefetch work, fits the 9 MB of opportunistic room K leaves, and B gets success.

The same failures occur at 7426fee (probe-7426fee.log), so this predates cycle 8. It is still a Stage-3 defect: at s3-base the follow moved every job in the apply's turn. The draft's notes cover a catch-up waiter's failure (cycle 3) and non-parked holders (cycle 8), not this case.

The cycle-7 RANK probes pass at HEAD in both visits (probe-head.log), so the cycle-7 fix holds.
issues.fix:
Failing tests first. Commit PROBE-C8-DROPPED, -DROPPED-KEEP and -DROPPED-LANE as R-SYN-11 tests in EngineSweepOrderTests.swift, with LaneDropVisit.allCases. Each asserts that K's user waiter is served, that B's waiter gets the answer the visit-first order gives it, and that A gets `.notFound` in both visits.

Then leave unjudged any candidate that still holds an id the copy does not list while a follow is owed. After the pre-phase this is the only way a candidate can still wait for the follow, and it costs one lookup per id. Owe a sweep for these jobs once the follow ends.

A verified prototype is in /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-orchestrator/s3f-probes-c8/correct/proto-skip-unlisted.diff. It adds `holdsUnlistedID`, `state.spaceSweepAfterFollow` and `scheduleSpaceSweepAfterFollow()` called at the end of `continueFollow`. With it, all 6 probes pass in both visits (probe-proto-skip.log). The whole Sync bundle passes: '✔ Test run with 421 tests in 53 suites passed after 23.817 seconds.'

The smaller change in proto-dropped.diff (re-queue without counting ahead) fixes DROPPED and DROPPED-KEEP but not DROPPED-LANE, so it is not enough.

Also correct the doc comment at EngineJobs.swift:697-698 and the draft text that claims the outcome matches the visit-first order.

So this cycle's restructure added about 3–5 ms and crossed C2 on a quiet host. This is not a load-only miss.

The committed benchmark passes in the same session at load 2.3–4.8: 'runs [5.434958, 5.508958, 5.410792]' (1 handle) and '[6.552458, 6.704792, 6.084333]' (2 handles). Its every-member-changed shape leaves nothing to judge after the follows, so it never sees this turn.

Two prototypes reduce but do not remove the overage:
- Splitting the turn, so a turn that followed judges nothing (proto-c2-split.diff): 9.05 / 10.30 ms best at load 2.3–2.5.

What remains is about 244 two-interest follows plus one collect, sort and scan of 10,000 in a single turn.
issues.fix:
Bound the sweep's work per turn under S3-R5. Give the pre-phase its own smaller follow budget (or count its follows against parksPerPump and readmissionsPerTurn). Judge in a separate turn after any follows (proto-c2-split.diff). Avoid re-scanning all 10,000 candidates with holdsMovedID on every sweep turn while a follow is owed: proto-c2-split-noscan.diff is one way, using copySerial; its invariant (no new space-parked holder until the next apply) needs a test.

Add this partial-change shape to BenchSync as a C2 benchmark: 1 member in 20 changed, so the owed holders number under followsPerTurn, measured with one handle and with two (c2Budget, best of three). Where possible, also assert the per-turn bound structurally in a unit test: follows per sweep turn, and judging only after following.

issues.problem:
The pre-phase follows only space-parked holders. Suppose a queued or downloading job C holds a moved id whose new content P is parked as prefetch work.

Timeline:
- The sweep judges P at its prefetch place, after R. R is re-queued, and the sweep's inline pump starts it.
- P is parked insufficientSpace, and P's prefetch waiter gets a shortage.
- The follow's visit then moves A (a user waiter) onto P. `relane` and `failFastJoiner` answer A with insufficientSpace(3 MB, 2.5 MB).
- If the follow had visited first, A and B would be served and R refused.

Every answer is true at the moment it is given (R really is in flight), and the fixer recorded the case. I did not write a probe for it, so it is not proven as a defect.
issues.fix: None required for this close-out beyond the record. If the dropped-id fix adds an owed sweep at the end of the follow, the fixer may note whether the same hook narrows this window.
